articles.title: Toys 'R' Us opens 160-plus stores, plans new NYC location
articles.summary: Toys "R" Us has opened more than 160 standalone US stores and is preparing to open a new location at New York City's Grand Central Terminal.
articles.body:
Nearly a decade after filing for bankruptcy and closing stores nationwide, Toys "R" Us is back, having opened more than 160 standalone locations across the United States as it continues rebuilding its presence in the country.

The company announced on Nov. 13 that its nationwide expansion, in partnership with Go! Retail Group, is complete , with more than 160 standalone locations now open. The rollout follows an expansion announced in September, when Toys "R" Us said it planned to open 120 new stores ahead of the holiday shopping season.

The retailer is also preparing to open a new location at New York City's Grand Central Terminal. A grand opening celebration is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, giving shoppers another place to find toys and holiday gifts ahead of Thanksgiving and Black Friday.

The event will begin at 10 a.m. ET at 89 East 42nd St. and feature an appearance by Geoffrey the Giraffe, the company's mascot. The first 50 customers in line will receive a special giveaway, according to Toys "R" Us.

What will the new Toys 'R' Us store sell?

The Grand Central Terminal location will feature a curated selection of toys, collectibles and gifts from popular brands and entertainment franchises, including Lego, Barbie, Hot Wheels, Pokémon and "KPop Demon Hunters."

The new store will serve commuters, tourists, collectors and other visitors to the Manhattan transportation hub, the company said.

Other standalone Toys "R" Us locations carry toys and collectibles from major brands, with select stores offering additional attractions such as candy shops, cafés and Creator Studios. The latter provides spaces for toy brands and content creators to film videos, unveil products and host events.

Toys "R" Us filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September 2017 while carrying about $5 billion in debt. The retailer liquidated its U.S. business and closed its remaining stores the following year.

The brand began returning to physical retail in 2019, opening smaller stores in New Jersey and Texas. Both locations eventually closed in 2021.

WHP Global acquired Toys "R" Us in 2021 and continued rebuilding the brand. In 2022, the company began opening Toys "R" Us shops inside Macy's stores nationwide. It later partnered with Go! Retail Group to expand its standalone store presence.

Where else can shoppers find Toys 'R' Us?

The retailer's U.S. presence extends beyond its standalone stores. Toys "R" Us has approximately 400 shops inside Macy's locations nationwide.

articles.title: FAA lifts ground stop flights, airline stocks fall
articles.summary: Airline stocks fell right before Friday's close after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop. Departing flights cannot ta...
articles.body:
The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop Friday evening after aging infrastructure forced the agency to halt outbound flights for hours, leaving passengers stranded at airports across the US.

The Federal Aviation Administration canceled the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, but delays are expected to extend into the weekend, with plans to prioritize aircraft that have more passengers on board.

Airline stocks fell right in post-market trading on Friday after the FAA ordered the nationwide ground stop. Departing flights could not take off, while flights already in the air continued to their destination.

At a press conference following the lift, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said aging infrastructure led to the ground stop.

"Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data, and they went down…and I shouldn't say they went down. They started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers, and because of that, we shut the system down," he said.

He added that there needs to be a complete overhaul of the system, including investing in new towers and airports, which he estimates will cost about $50 billion.

Shares of American Airlines ( AAL ), Southwest ( LUV ), JetBlue ( JBLU ), Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), and United Airlines ( UAL ) all moved lower on the news. The economic impact of the outage is unknown.

Around 5 p.m. Eastern, the FAA said in a statement on X that there was "a temporary telecommunications outage" and, "out of an abundance of caution," all flights had been halted. At the time, there were roughly 3,500 planes in the air, but more than 10,000 flights were disrupted.

This nationwide grounding was extremely rare. The last time that the FAA halted all US departures was in January of 2023 due to a system outage. Prior to that, traffic was halted after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Meanwhile, Microsoft said in a statement posted on X that the nationwide FAA ground stop was not related to any of its services. The tech giant apologized earlier on Friday for a software outage that left users unable to access Outlook email and other services, as the company worked to resolve the issues from Thursday into Friday.

articles.title: Mercado financeiro prevê juros de dois dígitos até 2030, ao longo dos dois mandatos de Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Expectativa consta de pesquisa realizada pelo BC com mais de 100 bancos. Quadro ocorre após déficits sucessivos nas contas públicas, a despeito da carga tributária recorde.
articles.summary: Expectativa consta de pesquisa realizada pelo BC com mais de 100 bancos. Quadro ocorre após déficits sucessivos nas contas públicas, a despeito da carga tributária recorde.
articles.body:
Mercado financeiro prevê juros de dois dígitos até 2030, ao longo dos dois mandatos de Lula — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No início do terceiro mandato do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, em 2023, o mercado financeiro projetava que a taxa básica de juros cairia para um dígito, abaixo de 10% ao ano, já em 2024.

Quase quatro anos depois, essa expectativa ficou mais distante. A previsão atual dos economistas dos bancos é de que a Selic não atingirá esse patamar nem em 2030.

➡️Se a previsão se confirmar, Lula passará o terceiro e o quarto mandatos inteiros com juros em dois dígitos (acima de 10% ao ano).

A expectativa dos economistas do mercado financeiro foi captada por meio de pesquisa realizada pelo Banco Central (BC) com mais de 100 instituições financeiras na semana passada.

Atualmente, a taxa está em 13,75% ao ano, o mesmo patamar do início de 2023. Em termos reais – ou seja, após o abatimento da inflação prevista para os próximos 12 meses –, o juro brasileiro está em 9,49% ao ano. É o maior patamar do mundo.

Até maio deste ano, o mercado acreditava que a taxa terminaria 2030 em 9,75% ao ano, em um dígito.

A partir daquele mês, os analistas passaram a projetar uma taxa de 10% ao ano.

A deterioração das expectativas do mercado nos últimos anos acontece após déficits sucessivos nas contas públicas .

A principal crítica é que as contas públicas continuaram no vermelho no terceiro mandato de Lula, mesmo com aumento de impostos e carga tributária recorde.

Durante o atual governo, a equipe econômica flexibilizou as metas das contas do governo , ampliando o espaço para despesas, fez uso do intervalo de tolerância previsto nas regras para as contas públicas e recorreu a receitas extraordinárias para cumprir os compromissos . Com autorização do Congresso, também realizou despesas por fora do limite estabelecido pela regra fiscal.

▶️O desempenho da atual gestão fiscal resultou em pressões inflacionárias, aumento dos juros e do endividamento público, em um processo de retroalimentação conhecido por economistas como "ciclo vicioso". Com a dívida em 82,9% do PIB pelo critério do BC e em 95,2% do PIB pelos cálculos do FMI, o Brasil registra um endividamento bem superior à média dos países emergentes.

De acordo com Jeferson Bittencourt, head de macroeconomia do ASA e ex-secretário do Tesouro Nacional, a piora na expectativa do mercado do terceiro para o quarto mandato é a "ausência do benefício da dúvida", ou seja, há uma descrença maior de que Lula vá promover um ajuste fiscal suficiente para estabilizar a dívida.

"No terceiro [mandato] se sabia que o novo governo trabalharia para revogar o teto de gastos, mas havia a dúvida sobre qual regra seria colocada no lugar. Para o quarto mandato, o novo arcabouço fiscal já é conhecido. Sabe-se que, quando cumprida à risca, ele oferece uma velocidade muito lenta de ajuste; que tanto o limite de despesas como a meta de superávit primário têm uma série de exceções; e que ante qualquer necessidade mais significativa novas exceções são adotadas, mesmo a regra tendo uma banda para acomodar choques", disse Bittencourt.

Solange Srour, diretora de macroeconomia para Brasil da gestora UBS GWM , disse que, diante do aumento dos juros nos Estados Unidos (que estabelece um piso maior para a taxa brasileira), considera díficil que a Selic volte a ficar abaixo de 10% ao ano nas condições atuais.

"O ambiente externo é apenas parte da explicação. No Brasil, a percepção mudou sobretudo porque aumentaram as dúvidas sobre a sustentabilidade da dívida pública. Com dívida elevada, despesas obrigatórias crescendo de forma estrutural e juros reais altos, cumprir metas fiscais de curto prazo não é suficiente se essas metas não estabilizam a relação dívida/PIB. O prêmio fiscal acaba aparecendo nos juros longos, no câmbio e nas expectativas de inflação e limita o espaço para uma queda mais rápida da Selic", diz a economista.

🔎A taxa de juros é definida pelo Banco Central com base no sistema de metas de inflação. O BC fixa a Selic olhando para frente, tendo por base as estimativas para o comportamento dos preços nos próximos anos.

Se as projeções estão em linha com as metas, pode manter ou baixar os juros. Se estão acima, a saída é elevar a taxa básica.

➡️A autoridade monetária esclarece, em sua página na internet , que a taxa básica da economia, a Selic, é de curto prazo.

Analistas observam que as taxas de juros negociadas no mercado para prazos mais longos (que servem de base para a venda de títulos públicos) reflete as expectativas dos agentes econômicos para gastos públicos e atividade, entre outros, e, consequentemente, para a inflação.

💰Juros altos têm consequências na economia e nas contas públicas. Eles tendem a frear o crédito, que fica mais caro, o consumo, o ritmo de atividade e o crescimento do emprego. Ao mesmo tempo, elevam as despesas com juros do setor público e pressionam o endividamento.

Trajetória da Selic, a taxa básica de juros, após decisão de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

▶️Para romper a atual dinâmica de pressão sobre a inflação e sobre endividamento público, possibilitando corte da Selic e da curva no mercado futuro, economistas e organismos financeiros internacionais avaliam que é preciso uma melhora das contas públicas — que registram déficits sucessivos há anos.

▶️O mercado financeiro é crítico da estratégia do governo federal do terceiro mandato de Lula de aumentar impostos para tentar reequilibrar as contas públicas, ao mesmo tempo que eleva gastos . Analistas pedem ênfase maior em cortes de despesas para que os juros possam recuar de forma sustentável no país, e conter a dívida pública.

"O ponto central é atacar os mecanismos que fazem a despesa obrigatória crescer automaticamente, em especial as regras de indexação e vinculação. Isso inclui rever a indexação de benefícios previdenciários e assistenciais ao salário mínimo, substituindo-a por uma referência compatível com a preservação do poder de compra, além de rever outras vinculações que fazem o gasto crescer de forma independente da situação fiscal", afirma Srour.

Ela defendeu, ainda, a revisão de benefícios fiscais "sem preservar exceções apenas porque determinados benefícios já existem há muito tempo ou têm grupos organizados em sua defesa".

Segundo Srour, também é preciso redesenhar e "melhorar a focalização" dos programas sociais, além de rever o MEI, o Simples Nacional e demais regimes especiais — preservando a formalização e a simplificação, mas reduzindo subsídios mal calibrados, distorções e tratamentos favorecidos sem justificativa econômica.

Economistas defendem o redesenho de programas como o MEI e o Simples Nacional — Foto: Divulgação/Sebrae

Para Bittencourt, melhorar a percepção do mercado financeiro passa pelo governo sinalizar maior disposição de sincronizar a política fiscal com a política monetária. Para isso, é necessário "mostrar compromisso com um ajuste nas contas que enderece a questão da sustentabilidade da dívida, retirando assim prêmio de risco da curva de juros".

Ele avaliou, ainda, que o pacote fiscal apresentado nesta semana ao Congresso Nacional inclui uma parte de ajuste permanente mais significativa, mas que não é uma mudança em relação à estratégia adotada até agora. Na prática, o foco permanece no aumento de receita, com um ajuste "bem menos significativo" pelo lado da despesa, acabando em 2030.

"Dado que a ajuda significativa para a melhora do primário não é uma mudança de estratégia, e a novidade no lado da despesa não traz contribuições significativas neste momento, não vejo o mercado mudando significativamente a visão sobre a taxa de juros ao longo do mandato", concluiu Bittencourt, do ASA.

Solange Srour concorda que o pacote não muda a trajetória fiscal, que é o que define os juros de curto e médio prazo . Segundo ela, o "mercado olha para a frente e enxerga uma dívida que continua crescendo rapidamente, sem âncora crível".

"A PEC que promete lidar de alguma forma com gastos obrigatórios e com limites às despesas fora do teto ainda não foi apresentada e assim não consigo avaliar se trará um choque de credibilidade suficiente para trazer os juros de fato para patamares mais baixos. Isso só ocorreria, no meu entender, com mudanças estruturais no gasto obrigatório, não com medidas que aumentem receitas ou a base de gastos passível de contingenciamento", concluiu a economista.

articles.title: FAA Ground Stop: What to do if your flight was delayed or canceled on Friday
articles.summary: What to do if your flight was cancelled or delayed by the FAA's national ground stop on Friday
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

If you were traveling on Friday and your flight was canceled or delayed by the hours-long stoppage affecting all departing flights in the U.S., you may be able to recoup some money, including a full refund in some cases.

A good first step is to call your airline. Check the airline's website and app for information about your options. For instance, United Airlines and Delta, two of the nation's largest airlines, put up banners on their websites on Friday evening with links to pages with directions on how to rebook for free or cancel.

A government-ordered ground stop is extremely unusual, and it's possible airlines will have some leeway in their obligations under these circumstances. Again, contact your airline for information.

Travelers delayed by the national ground stop should:

Verify your flight status with your airline . Delays will filter through the system for days.

Monitor your airline's mobile app for updates . Gates, connecting flights, and departure times are likely to change.

Some airlines have temporarily canceled service . Make sure you know when your flight will be rescheduled.

Know refund options available to you . Federal rules entitle you to a full refund if your flight is canceled or significantly delayed.

Rebook your flight through your airline's app . Rather than waiting in a long line, try rebooking your flight through an app.

Document receipts . Save every expense related to the delay for possible travel insurance reimbursement.

Here are major airline customer service numbers:

Southwest: 1-800-I-FLY-SWA (1-800-435-9792)

Alaska: 1-800-ALASKAAIR (1-800-252-7522)

Under normal government rules, travelers are entitled to a refund if the airline canceled your flight, regardless of the reason, according to the Department of Transportation . You are also entitled to a refund if the airline delays a flight. You do not have to accept travel credits, vouchers, or other forms of compensation. The delay typically needs to be at least three hours for domestic trips and six hours for international itineraries.

If you do not want to travel due to the disruption, you should ask your airline for a refund to your original payment method. Your refund should come in a week if you paid with a credit card. It could take three weeks for other payment methods.

Airlines are not always obligated to offer lodging, food, or other assistance for every delay or cancellation.

Nearly 14,500 flights were grounded Friday after an order from the Federal Aviation Administration. The halt to air travel was apparently caused by a telecommunications outage caused by a software update to Air Route Traffic Control Centers, the Associated Press reported. Homeland Security and government officials said that there was no indication of "nefarious acts" related to the telecommunications outage.

The travel interruption ended shortly before 9 p.m. Eastern time Friday.

Flights have resumed, though a chain reaction of delays and cancellations is expected to filter through the national flight system.

The interruption was the third nationwide ground stop in history, following a 2023 system failure and the September 11 attacks.

articles.title: Nvidia spy scandal: What Jensen Huang told top executives about his relationship with Alice Huang
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled some of the chipmaker's senior executives about his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.
articles.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled some of the chipmaker's senior executives about his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. He portrayed their interactions as routine business dealings, despite having an affair with her, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters.Among the executives Huang communicated with were general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld. In two separate messages sent in October, Huang told them that his interactions with Alice Huang were part of standard business dealings with customers. He also described his engagement with her company, Megaspeed International, as routine in other communications, people told Reuters.Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on the condition that the messages would not be quoted verbatim. The news agency is the first to report on the correspondence.The two people said Huang had addressed questions about his relationship with Alice Huang on two occasions, during the autumn of 2025 and again in October 2026, after press queries brought the matter to the attention of some Nvidia leaders. On both occasions, he described their interactions as appropriate. Reuters reviewed only the October messages and not the exchanges from 2025.Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed International, an Nvidia customer, was under investigation by the US over suspicions that she may have been spying for China. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share the same surname but are not related.Earlier questions about meetings with Alice HuangHuang's interactions with Alice Huang had come under scrutiny following a New York Times article published in October last year, which highlighted their public meetings. According to the two people, Huang subsequently discussed the possibility of taking legal action against the newspaper.The article had also prompted him to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about his interactions with Alice Huang. However, he did not describe the relationship as an affair, the people said.Neither Huang nor Nvidia eventually sued the newspaper. A spokesperson for the New York Times said it had received no legal demand.It remains unclear when the relationship became intimate. Photographs posted online and verified by Reuters show the two together in the US, China and elsewhere, dating back to December 2023.Board orders independent probeOn November 10, Nvidia's independent board members announced that they had appointed Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation. The move followed reports by the New York Times and Wall Street Journal about Huang's relationships with Alice Huang and US authorities' suspicions that she was spying for China.Beijing has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. Reuters has not independently verified whether she was working on behalf of the Chinese government.In an interview with Bloomberg published on October 29, Jensen Huang said the US government had not informed him about its suspicions concerning Alice Huang.Huang exits Nvidia Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday. His departure marks a dramatic fall from the top of the chip industry, where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent artificial intelligence boom.In a statement earlier this week, he apologised for being unfaithful to his wife and disappointing the company. However, he did not specifically name Alice Huang.The revelations also follow reports of other relationships. The New York Times reported earlier this week that Huang had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee. Reuters reported on Thursday that he had another intimate relationship with a different Nvidia employee.Nvidia's stock has fallen more than 30% from its October 6 closing high, wiping out more than $1.8 trillion from its market capitalisation, taking the figure below $4 trillion mark for the first time.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Mumbai office boy earning Rs 3,500 a month faces Rs 1.46 crore tax assessment; alleges ex-employer misused KYC documents to obtain second PAN, ITAT quashes demand over invalid service of notice
articles.summary: A man who says he worked as an office boy for Rs 3,500 a month found himself facing an income-tax assessment of nearly Rs 1.47 crore after the tax
articles.body: A man who says he worked as an office boy for Rs 3,500 a month found himself facing an income-tax assessment of nearly Rs 1.47 crore after the tax department linked him to a pharmaceutical business and transactions recorded in its bank account. His defence was that he had never run the business and that his former employer had allegedly misused his signatures and identity documents.The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, did not decide whether those allegations were true. Instead, it examined a more fundamental question: had the Income Tax Department validly served the notice that allowed it to reopen his assessment in the first place?In its September 21, 2026, order, the tribunal ruled that the department had failed to establish valid service and quashed the reassessment. The additions made in the proceedings consequently could not survive.What the case is aboutThe Income Tax Department initiated reassessment proceedings against a man after receiving information about transactions associated with a pharma company, described in the information available to the tax authorities as the man’s proprietary concern.The bank account records showed debit entries of Rs 1,27,62,500 and credit entries of Rs 18,85,000. The Assessing Officer treated the debit amount as unexplained expenditure under Section 69C of the Income Tax Act and the credit amount as unexplained income under Section 68. The assessment was completed under Sections 144 and 147, and the AO pegged the man’s total income at Rs 1,46,57,500.The assessee disputed the department's case on several fronts. According to his submissions, he had worked as an office boy for an employer from September 2009 for approximately 18 months, earning Rs 3,500 a month. He said he had provided signatures and KYC documents believing they were required for employment and security purposes.He alleged that the employer had used those documents to obtain another PAN without his knowledge. The man maintained that he had neither operated the pharma company nor undertaken the transactions in question. These remained his allegations; the tribunal did not establish that his former employer had misused his documents.The immediate legal dispute concerned a notice issued under Section 148 on March 27, 2019, which the man said he had never received.Why ITAT ruled in favour of the ex-office boyThe tribunal examined the department's records and found that the notice sent to an address in Bandra East had remained unserved. The department subsequently relied on affixture, or pasting the notice on a premises in Bhiwandi.The problem was that the department had not established any connection between the man and the locked room where the notice was pasted. Its own records indicated that he did not reside at the Bhiwandi address.The tribunal observed: “Affixture on the door of any locked room, without establishing that it was the residence or business premises of the assessee, cannot constitute service upon him merely because a departmental officer had gone there and pasted a notice.”The department eventually obtained the man’s Vile Parle address and email details through enquiries from TransUnion CIBIL. A show-cause notice sent on November 22, 2019, reached him, and he responded five days later, disputing the PAN and denying knowledge of the company.The tribunal noted: “The final show-cause notice dated 22.11.2019 was thus the first communication which, on the basis of the material before us, is shown to have actually reached the assessee.”The man had raised objections before the assessment was completed. The tribunal held that his subsequent cooperation could not retrospectively cure the failure to serve the original notice. It stated: “Participation after raising a timely objection cannot retrospectively convert affixture at an unrelated premises into valid service.”The judges concluded that valid service of the notice was essential for the department to assume jurisdiction over the reassessment. Their order stated: “The assessment order passed under section 144 read with section 147 is, therefore, invalid and is hereby quashed.”The additions of Rs 1,27,62,500 and Rs 18,85,000 consequently fell with the reassessment. The appeal was allowed.The tribunal expressly left undecided the alleged misuse of the man’s PAN, signatures and KYC documents, as well as the genuineness of the underlying transactions, because the reassessment was invalid on the jurisdictional ground.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit costs him Rs 900 crore: How much wealth does he have left?
articles.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s exit from the chipmaking giant may cost him a whopping $108 million in stock awards!
articles.body: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s exit from the chipmaking giant may cost him a whopping $108 million in stock awards!While the amount sounds huge, it is only a tiny fraction of the massive fortune he has built over 33 years at the company. With an estimated net worth of $144.5 billion, the Nvidia co-founder is set to give up just 0.07% of his wealth following his exit.Huang’s departure comes at a time when Nvidia shares have taken a hit.The company’s market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 following news of his resignation. However, despite the fall, Huang’s biggest source of wealth remains his existing shareholding, valued at around $135 billion.The $108 million he is set to lose comes from stock awards that have not yet vested. Under Nvidia’s equity compensation policy, executives forfeit their unvested restricted stock units (RSUs) when they leave the company.Huang held around 346,000 such units and was expected to receive about 310,000 shares under the company’s equity incentive plan, provided certain performance targets were met.Following his exit, he will forfeit these unvested awards.Jensen Huang has already slipped out of the top 10 of Forbes' richest people list, with his wealth declining by $2.8 billion, or 1.97%. According to Nvidia's annual report and proxy statement for fiscal year 2026, Huang received total compensation of $36,343,830 during the year, down from $49.87 million in the previous financial year.His compensation package included a base salary of around $1.5 million, stock awards worth approximately $24.8 million and $6 million in non-equity incentive plan compensation. The remaining amount was classified as other compensation.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Where does Huang's $144.5 billion fortune come from?Almost all of Huang's wealth is tied to Nvidia shares. Unlike several other technology leaders, he has built his fortune mainly through owning the company's stock rather than stock options or other executive benefits.He owns around 812 million Nvidia shares, worth approximately $135 billion at Thursday's closing price. This makes him the company's largest individual shareholder. His holding represents less than 5% of Nvidia, while his voting stake stands at around 3.5%.According to Bloomberg's wealth index, Nvidia shares account for nearly 97% of his total fortune.His holdings are spread across shares owned directly by him, family trusts and holding companies. His charitable foundation separately holds around 59 million Nvidia shares, valued at more than $9 billion at current prices.Despite his substantial holding, Huang does not have special voting rights because Nvidia has only one class of shares.His salary and other cash payments form only a small part of his wealth. He received around $7.5 million in cash compensation in each of the past two years.Huang has already pocketed $3 billionAlthough Huang has held on to most of his Nvidia shares, he has sold around $3 billion worth of stock since the company went public in 1999, according to Capital IQ data and company filings.For most of his time as chief executive, his annual share sales remained relatively small, rarely crossing a few hundred million dollars. That changed as Nvidia's valuation climbed during the AI boom.Huang sold around $713 million worth of shares in 2024, followed by approximately $1 billion in 2025. These sales were made through pre-arranged trading plans as Nvidia's market value crossed $3 trillion and later $5 trillion.He has not sold any shares so far this year, according to the data.Can Huang turn his shares into cashWith Huang no longer leading Nvidia, attention is also turning to whether he will begin selling more of his shares. However, offloading such a large holding may not be easy.His share transactions could be affected by potential lengthy legal investigations into his relationship with a Chinese executive at a major Nvidia customer. Analysts at William Blair have described the matter as a “significant overhang on Nvidia shares in the near term”.There are also restrictions on when he can trade because of information he may have received while heading the company.Jesse Fried, a corporate governance expert at Harvard, said Huang would have to wait until material negative information that could affect Nvidia's share price became public before selling.“Huang can start selling as soon as any negative material non-public information he learned while CEO is disclosed,” Fried said.He is “OK to sell knowing undisclosed positive information, because [he] can’t profit from that,” Fried said.Nvidia's results next Tuesday could clear the way for Huang to start selling, provided he does not hold any other insider information, lawyers said.The size of his holding is another challenge. His 812 million shares are equivalent to around six days of Nvidia's total trading volume. Selling a large number of shares at once could put pressure on the stock price, meaning any sale would probably have to be spread over several months.Huang has also avoided borrowing against his Nvidia shares. Unlike some other technology billionaires, he has not pledged his stock as collateral for loans, as Nvidia does not allow its executives to do so.Money habits form by age 7.
